verdict.rationale: Google documents a public RESTful Calendar API, reachable by HTTP or client libraries, that 'exposes most of the features available in the Google Calendar Web interface.' The v3 reference covers calendar creation, events, recurring instances, ACLs, free/busy, watch and push notifications, and incremental sync. A machine-readable discovery document also exists, even though the OpenAPI and llms.txt probes at developers.google.com returned 404. missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of driving the product via the API, full feature parity with the web UI (docs say 'most').

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can drive the product through a documented public API

citations.quote: The Google Calendar API is a RESTful API that can be accessed through explicit HTTP calls or using the Google Client Libraries.
The API exposes most of the features available in the Google Calendar Web interface.
Returns free/busy information for a set of calendars.
